title.zh: 卷五十二 列傳第二: 后妃下
title.raw: 卷五十二 列傳第二: 后妃下 Volume 52 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts 2

meta.sourceNote: Body restored from Wikisource juan 52 to match the ChineseNotes chapter heading. The previous Wikisource import used the file number instead of the traditional juan.

sentences.zh: 玄宗元獻皇后楊氏，弘農華陰人。

translations.literal: Empress Yuanxian of Emperor Xuanzong, née Yang, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanxian of Emperor Xuanzong, the Yang clan, came from Huayin in Hongnong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖士達，隋納言，天授中，以則天母族，追封士達為鄭王，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Shida was Director of the Secretariat under the Sui; in the Tianshou era, because he was of Empress Wu's maternal clan, Shida was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng and given the posthumous title of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Shida had served the Sui as Director of the Secretariat. In the Tianshou period, as a kinsman on Empress Wu's mother's side, he was posthumously created Prince of Zheng and honored as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父知慶，左千牛將軍，贈太尉、鄭國公。

translations.literal: Her father Zhiqing was Left Colonel of the Thousand-Ox Guard and was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhiqing, Left Colonel of the Thousand-Ox Guard, was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant and Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 后景雲元年八月選入太子宮。

translations.literal: The empress was selected into the crown prince's palace in the eighth month of the first year of Jingyun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jingyun 1, she was chosen for the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主用事，尤忌東宮。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Taiping held power and was especially hostile to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was then in power and bore special enmity toward the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宮中左右持兩端，而潛附太平者，必陰伺察，事雖纖芥，皆聞于上，太子心不自安。

translations.literal: Those in the palace who straddled both sides, yet secretly sided with Taiping, would surely spy in secret; though matters were as fine as a mustard seed, all reached the throne, and the crown prince's heart was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants hedged their bets, and those who secretly favored Taiping watched in the shadows. Even the smallest matters reached the emperor's ears, and the crown prince lived in constant unease.

sentences.zh: 后時方娠，太子密謂張說曰：「用事者不欲吾多息胤，恐禍及此婦人，其如之何？」

translations.literal: The empress was then pregnant. The crown prince secretly said to Zhang Yue: "Those in power do not wish me to have many heirs; I fear calamity will reach this woman—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress was pregnant. The crown prince confided to Zhang Yue, "Those in power do not want me to have many sons. I fear harm will reach this woman. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 密令說懷去胎藥而入。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered Zhang Yue to take abortifacient medicine inside his robes and enter.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Zhang Yue to carry abortifacient medicine inside his robes and bring it in.

sentences.zh: 太子于曲室躬自煮藥，醺然似寐，夢神人覆鼎。

translations.literal: In a side chamber the crown prince personally brewed the medicine; drowsy, he seemed to sleep, and dreamed of a divine being covering the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: In a side room the crown prince brewed the medicine himself. Growing drowsy as if asleep, he dreamed that a divine being covered the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 既寤如夢，如是者三。

translations.literal: When he awoke it was as in the dream; this happened three times.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, it was exactly as in the dream—and so three times.

sentences.zh: 太子異之，告說。

translations.literal: The crown prince thought it strange and told Zhang Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince found it strange and told Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「天命也，無宜他慮。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said: "It is Heaven's mandate; there is no cause for other concerns."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said, "This is Heaven's decree. Give no thought to anything else."

sentences.zh: 既而太平誅，後果生肅宗。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Taiping was executed, and the empress indeed bore Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Taiping was put to death, and the empress did bear Emperor Suzong.

sentences.zh: 太子妃王氏無子，后班在下，后不敢母肅宗。

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort, Lady Wang, had no son; the empress's rank stood below hers, and the empress did not dare claim Suzong as her own.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Princess Wang had no son. The empress ranked below her and did not dare claim Suzong as her own child.

sentences.zh: 王妃撫鞠，慈甚所生。

translations.literal: The royal consort reared and nurtured him, as lovingly as if he were her own.
translations.idiomatic: The princess consort raised him with a tenderness equal to a birth mother's.

sentences.zh: 開元中，肅宗為忠王，后為妃，又生甯親公主。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era Suzong was Prince of Zhong, and the empress became his consort; she also bore Princess Ningqin.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyuan, when Suzong was Prince of Zhong, she became his consort and later bore Princess Ningqin.

sentences.zh: 張說以舊恩特承寵異，說亦奇忠王儀錶，心知運曆所鐘，故甯親公主降說子垍。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, by reason of old favor, received special grace; he also marveled at Prince Zhong's bearing and knew in his heart that the mandate of fortune was upon him, and so Princess Ningqin was given in marriage to Zhang Yue's son Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, owing to old ties, enjoyed exceptional favor. He also admired Prince Zhong's bearing and sensed that destiny favored him, so Princess Ningqin was married to his son Qi.

sentences.zh: 開元十七年，后薨，葬細柳原，玄宗命說為志文，其銘云：「石獸澀兮綠苔黏，宿草殘兮白露霑。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaiyuan the empress died and was buried at Xiliuyuan. Emperor Xuanzong ordered Zhang Yue to compose the epitaph; the inscription reads: "Stone beasts grow rough; green moss clings.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 17 the empress died and was buried at Xiliuyuan. Xuanzong had Zhang Yue write the epitaph, which reads, "Stone beasts roughen; green moss clings.

sentences.zh: 園寢閉兮脂粉膩，不知何年開鏡奩。」

translations.literal: The garden tomb is shut; rouge and powder congeal—who knows in what year the mirror casket will open again."
translations.idiomatic: The garden tomb is sealed; rouge and powder thicken—who knows what year the mirror case will open again."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，忠王立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Prince Zhong was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, Prince Zhong was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 至德元年，肅宗即位于靈武。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide, Suzong ascended the throne at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 1, Suzong took the throne at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 二載五月，玄宗在蜀，誥曰：「聖人垂范，是推顧復之恩；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, while Xuanzong was in Shu, an edict proclaimed: "The sage sets an example and thereby extends the grace of nurturing;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year, with Xuanzong in Shu, an edict declared, "The sage sets the pattern and extends the grace of nurturing;

sentences.zh: 王者建極，抑有追尊之禮。

translations.literal: the king who establishes the supreme norm likewise has rites of posthumous elevation.
translations.idiomatic: the ruler who establishes the supreme norm likewise observes rites of posthumous elevation.

sentences.zh: 蓋母以子貴，德以諡尊。

translations.literal: Thus the mother is honored through the son, and virtue is exalted through the posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: A mother is honored through her son, and virtue is exalted through the posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 故妃弘農楊氏，特稟坤靈，久厘陰教。

translations.literal: Therefore Consort Yang of Hongnong was endowed with the spirit of Earth and long cultivated the teachings of the feminine.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang of Hongnong was endowed with Earth's spirit and long upheld the feminine teachings of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 往以續塗山之慶，降華渚之祥。

translations.literal: In former times she continued the blessing of Tushan; she descended with the auspice of Huazhu.
translations.idiomatic: Once she continued the blessing of Tushan and descended with the auspice of Huazhu.

sentences.zh: 誕發異圖，載光帝業。

translations.literal: She gave birth to a prodigious heir and brought glory to the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: She bore an extraordinary heir and brought glory to the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 而冊命猶闕，幽靈尚牴。

translations.literal: Yet investiture was still lacking, and the hidden spirit remained unreconciled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet formal investiture was still lacking, and her spirit remained unreconciled.

sentences.zh: 夏王繼統，方軫陽城之恩；

translations.literal: When the Xia king succeeded to the line, he mourned the kindness of Yangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia king succeeded to the throne, he mourned the kindness owed to Yangcheng;

sentences.zh: 漢後褒榮，庶協昭靈之稱。

translations.literal: when the Han empress was honored, it was hoped to accord with the title of Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: when the Han empress was honored, it was hoped to accord with the title Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 宜於彼追冊為元獻太后。」

translations.literal: She should there be posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Dowager Yuanxian."
translations.idiomatic: Let her there be posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Dowager Yuanxian."

sentences.zh: 寶應二年正月，祔葬泰陵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Baoying, she was enshrined and buried at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Baoying 2, she was enshrined and buried at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 肅宗張皇后，本南陽西鄂人，後徙家昭應。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang of Emperor Suzong was originally from Xi'e in Nanyang; her family later moved to Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang of Suzong was originally from Xi'e in Nanyang; her family later moved to Zhaoying.

sentences.zh: 祖母竇氏，玄宗母昭成皇太后之妹也。

translations.literal: Her grandmother, Lady Dou, was the younger sister of Empress Zhaocheng, Xuanzong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandmother Lady Dou was the younger sister of Empress Zhaocheng, Xuanzong's mother.

sentences.zh: 昭成為天后所殺，玄宗幼失所恃，為竇姨鞠養。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng was killed by Empress Wu; Xuanzong, young, lost his mother and was reared by Aunt Dou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng was killed by Empress Wu. Xuanzong, bereft of his mother in youth, was raised by Aunt Dou.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，封鄧國夫人，恩渥甚隆。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era she was enfeoffed as Lady of Deng and received lavish favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun period she was created Lady of Deng and received lavish favor.

sentences.zh: 其子去惑、去疑、去奢、去逸，皇姨弟也，皆至大官。

translations.literal: Her sons Quhuo, Quyi, Qushe, and Quyi were maternal cousins of the emperor and all reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Quhuo, Quyi, Qushe, and Quyi were the emperor's maternal cousins and all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 去盈尚玄宗女常芬公主。

translations.literal: Quyi married Princess Changfen, Xuanzong's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Quyi married Xuanzong's daughter, Princess Changfen.

sentences.zh: 去逸生后，天寶中，選入太子宮為良娣。

translations.literal: Quyi's daughter became the empress; in the Tianbao era she was chosen into the crown prince's palace as a worthy consort.
translations.idiomatic: Quyi's daughter became the empress. In the Tianbao era she was chosen for the crown prince's palace as Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 后弟清，又尚大寧郡主。

translations.literal: The empress's younger brother Qing also married Princess Daning.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's younger brother Qing also married Princess Daning.

sentences.zh: 后辯惠豐碩，巧中上旨。

translations.literal: The empress was eloquent, clever, and ample of form, and skillfully hit upon the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was eloquent, clever, and full-figured, and skillfully matched the sovereign's wishes.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，太子與良娣俱從，車駕渡渭，百姓遮道請留太子收復長安。

translations.literal: When the Rebellion of An Lushan broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu; the crown prince and Worthy Consort both followed. As the imperial carriage crossed the Wei, the common people blocked the road and begged the crown prince to remain and recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan's rebellion broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu. The crown prince and Worthy Consort followed. At the Wei crossing the people blocked the road and begged the crown prince to stay and recover Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 肅宗性仁孝，以上皇播越，不欲違離左右。

translations.literal: Suzong was by nature filial and could not bear to leave the retired emperor's side, since the sovereign had been driven into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was naturally filial. With the retired emperor cast into exile, he could not bear to leave his side.

sentences.zh: 宦者李靖忠啟太子請留，良娣贊成之，白于玄宗。

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Jingzhong urged the crown prince to remain; Worthy Consort supported this and reported it to Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Jingzhong urged the crown prince to stay. Worthy Consort supported him and reported it to Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 太子如靈武，時賊已陷京師，從官單寮，道路多虞。

translations.literal: The crown prince went to Lingwu. By then the rebels had taken the capital; his followers were few, and the roads held many dangers.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince went on to Lingwu. The rebels had already taken the capital; his retinue was thin and the roads perilous.

sentences.zh: 每太子次舍宿止，良娣必居其前。

translations.literal: Whenever the crown prince halted to lodge, Worthy Consort always took the place ahead of him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the crown prince stopped to lodge, Worthy Consort always took the place ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「捍禦非婦人之事，何以居前？」

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "Defense is not a woman's task—why take the fore?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "Defense is no woman's work. Why go ahead?"

sentences.zh: 良娣曰：「今大家跋履險難，兵衛非多，恐有倉卒，妾自當之，大家可由後而出，庶幾無患。」

translations.literal: Worthy Consort said: "Now Your Majesty is treading peril and hardship, and the guard is not large; I fear something sudden. Let me meet it myself, and Your Majesty may go out from the rear—then perhaps there will be no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Consort said, "Your Majesty now treads danger with few guards. I fear a sudden attack. Let me meet it first; Your Majesty can leave by the rear. Then we may escape harm."

sentences.zh: 及至靈武，產子，三日起，縫戰士衣。

translations.literal: When they reached Lingwu she gave birth; on the third day she rose and sewed garments for the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu she gave birth. On the third day she rose and sewed clothing for the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 太子勞之曰：「產忌作勞，安可容易？」

translations.literal: The crown prince comforted her, saying: "Childbirth forbids labor—how can you take it lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince urged her, "Childbirth forbids exertion. How can you take this so lightly?"

sentences.zh: 後曰：「此非妾自養之時，須辦大家事。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "This is not the time for me to nurse myself; I must attend to Your Majesty's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "This is no time to tend myself. I must see to Your Majesty's affairs."

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，冊為淑妃。

translations.literal: When Suzong ascended the throne, she was invested as Cultivated Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, she was invested as Cultivated Consort.

sentences.zh: 贈父太僕卿去逸左僕射，母竇氏封義章縣主，姊李曇妻封清河郡夫人，妹師師封郕國夫人。

translations.literal: Her father Quyi was posthumously honored as Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and Left Vice Director; her mother Lady Dou was created Lady of Yizhang; her elder sister, wife of Li Yan, was created Lady of Qinghe; her younger sister Shishi was created Lady of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Quyi was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and Left Vice Director; her mother Lady Dou was created Lady of Yizhang; her elder sister, Li Yan's wife, Lady of Qinghe; her younger sister Shishi, Lady of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年四月，冊為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Qianyuan she was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Qianyuan 1 she was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 弟駙馬都尉清加特進、太常卿，同正，封范陽郡公。

translations.literal: Her younger brother, Chief Commandant of the Empress's Household Qing, was given special advancement as Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments with concurrent rank, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Qing, Chief Commandant of the Empress's Household, was specially advanced to Grand Master of Imperial Entertainments with concurrent rank and enfeoffed Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 皇后寵遇專房，與中官李輔國持權禁中，干預政事，請謁過當，帝頗不悅，無如之何。

translations.literal: The empress's favor filled the inner chambers alone; with the palace eunuch Li Fuguo she held power within the forbidden precincts, intervened in government, and requests and audiences exceeded propriety. The emperor was quite displeased but could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress enjoyed exclusive favor. With the eunuch Li Fuguo she wielded power inside the palace, meddled in affairs of state, and petitions and audiences exceeded all bounds. The emperor was deeply displeased but powerless.

sentences.zh: 後於光順門受外命婦朝，親蠶苑中，內外命婦相見，儀注甚盛。

translations.literal: Later at Guangshun Gate she received outer court ladies in audience, and personally performed the mulberry rite in the garden; inner and outer court ladies met, and the ceremonial was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Later she received outer-court ladies in audience at Guangshun Gate and personally performed the mulberry rite in the garden. Inner and outer ladies met in ceremony of great splendor.

sentences.zh: 先在靈武時，太子弟建甯王倓為后誣譖而死。

translations.literal: Earlier at Lingwu, the crown prince's younger brother Prince of Jianning, Chen, had died after being slandered by the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Lingwu, the crown prince's younger brother Prince Chen of Jianning had died after the empress slandered him.

sentences.zh: 自是太子憂懼，常恐后之構禍，乃以恭遜取容，后以建寧之隙，常欲危之。

translations.literal: From then on the crown prince lived in worry and fear, constantly dreading that the empress would contrive disaster; he therefore won favor through humble deference, while the empress, because of the rift over Jianning, constantly sought to endanger him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the crown prince lived in fear that the empress would contrive his ruin. He won favor through humble deference, while she, because of the Jianning affair, constantly sought to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 張后生二子：興王佋、定王侗。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang bore two sons: Prince of Xing, Zhou, and Prince of Ding, Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang bore two sons: Prince Zhou of Xing and Prince Tong of Ding.

sentences.zh: 興王早薨，侗又孩幼，故儲位獲安。

translations.literal: Prince of Xing died early, and Tong was still an infant; therefore the heir's position remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xing died young and Tong was still an infant, so the heir's position held firm.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年四月，肅宗大漸，后與內官朱輝光、馬英俊、啖廷瑤、陳仙甫等謀立越王係，矯詔召太子入侍疾。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Baoying, as Suzong lay gravely ill, the empress plotted with inner officials Zhu Huiguang, Ma Yingjun, Dan Tingyao, and Chen Xianfu to establish Prince of Yue, Xi; a forged edict summoned the crown prince to attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Baoying 1, as Suzong lay dying, the empress plotted with the inner officials Zhu Huiguang, Ma Yingjun, Dan Tingyao, and Chen Xianfu to install Prince Xi of Yue. A forged edict summoned the crown prince to the bedside.

sentences.zh: 中官程元振、李輔國知其謀，及太子入，二人以難告，請太子在飛龍廄。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Cheng Yuanzhen and Li Fuguo learned of the plot; when the crown prince entered, the two told him of the danger and asked that he stay at Feilong Stable.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Cheng Yuanzhen and Li Fuguo learned of the plot. When the crown prince arrived, they warned him and asked him to remain at Feilong Stable.

sentences.zh: 元振率禁軍收越王，捕硃輝光等。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen led the imperial guard to seize Prince of Yue and arrest Zhu Huiguang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen led the imperial guard to seize Prince of Yue and arrest Zhu Huiguang and the rest.

sentences.zh: 俄而肅宗崩，太子監國，遂移后於別殿，幽崩。

translations.literal: Soon Suzong died; the crown prince supervised the state and moved the empress to a separate hall, where she died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Suzong died. The crown prince took charge of the state, moved the empress to a separate hall, and she died in confinement.

sentences.zh: 誅馬英俊，女道士許靈素配流，山人申大芝賜死，駙馬都尉清貶硤州司馬，弟延和郡主婿鴻臚卿潛貶郴州司馬，舅鴻臚卿竇履信貶道州刺史。

translations.literal: Ma Yingjun was executed; the Daoist nun Xu Lingsu was banished; the recluse Shen Dazhi was sentenced to death; Chief Commandant Qing was demoted to prefectural aide in Xiazhou; Qing's younger brother, son-in-law of Princess Yanhe and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Qian, was demoted to prefectural aide in Chenzhou; maternal uncle Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Dou Lüxin was demoted to prefect of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yingjun was executed; the Daoist Xu Lingsu was banished; the recluse Shen Dazhi was put to death; Chief Commandant Qing was demoted to aide in Xia Prefecture; his brother Qian, Director of Imperial Sacrifices and Princess Yanhe's son-in-law, to aide in Chen Prefecture; and their uncle Dou Lüxin, also Director of Imperial Sacrifices, to prefect of Dao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 肅宗韋妃。

translations.literal: Consort Wei of Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei of Emperor Suzong.

sentences.zh: 父元珪，兗州都督。

translations.literal: Her father Yuanqi was military governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yuanqi was military governor of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 肅宗為忠王時，納為孺人，及升儲位，為太子妃，生兗王僴、絳王佺、永和公主、永穆公主。

translations.literal: When Suzong was Prince of Zhong he took her as a lady; when he was elevated as heir apparent she became crown princess and bore Prince of Yan, Xian, Prince of Jiang, Quan, Princess Yonghe, and Princess Yongmu.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was Prince of Zhong he took her as a lady; when he became heir apparent she became crown princess and bore Prince Xian of Yan, Prince Quan of Jiang, Princess Yonghe, and Princess Yongmu.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，宰相李林甫不利於太子，妃兄堅為刑部尚書，林甫羅織，起柳勣之獄，堅連坐得罪，兄弟並賜死。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era Chancellor Li Linfu was hostile to the crown prince; the consort's elder brother Jian was Minister of Justice, and Linfu fabricated charges, raising the case of Liu Ji; Jian was implicated and punished, and the brothers were all sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao, Chancellor Li Linfu was hostile to the crown prince. The consort's brother Jian, Minister of Justice, was framed in the Liu Ji affair; Jian was implicated and the brothers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 太子懼，上表自理，言與妃情義不睦，請離婚，玄宗慰撫之，聽離。

translations.literal: The crown prince feared this and submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying that he and the consort were not on affectionate terms and requesting divorce; Xuanzong comforted him and granted the separation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, in fear, submitted a memorial clearing himself, saying he and the consort were not close and asking for divorce. Xuanzong comforted him and granted it.

sentences.zh: 妃遂削髮被尼服，居禁中佛舍。

translations.literal: The consort then shaved her head and wore nun's robes, dwelling in a Buddhist hall within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The consort shaved her head, put on nun's robes, and lived in a Buddhist hall within the palace.

sentences.zh: 西京失守，妃亦陷賊。

translations.literal: When the Western Capital fell, the consort also fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Capital fell, she too was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，薨於京城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide she died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 she died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 肅宗章敬皇后吳氏，坐父事沒入掖庭。

translations.literal: Empress Zhangjing of Emperor Suzong, née Wu, entered the palace women because of her father's case.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhangjing of Suzong, née Wu, entered the palace women because of her father's offense.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年，玄宗幸忠王邸，見王服御蕭然，傍無媵侍，命將軍高力士選掖庭宮人以賜之，而吳后在籍中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong visited Prince Zhong's residence, saw the prince's furnishings sparse and no attendant ladies at his side, and ordered General Gao Lishi to select palace women from the inner quarters to give him; Wu was among those on the register.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 Xuanzong visited Prince Zhong's residence, found his furnishings sparse and no attendant ladies beside him, and ordered General Gao Lishi to choose palace women from the inner quarters as gifts. Wu was on the register.

sentences.zh: 容止端麗，性多謙抑，寵遇益隆。

translations.literal: Her bearing was upright and lovely, and her nature very modest; favor toward her grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Her bearing was graceful and her nature deeply modest; favor toward her steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 明年，生代宗皇帝。

translations.literal: The next year she bore Emperor Daizong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year she bore Emperor Daizong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年薨，葬於春明門外。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year she died and was buried outside Chunming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year she died and was buried outside Chunming Gate.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位之年十二月，群臣以肅宗山陵有期，准禮以先太后祔陵廟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the year Daizong ascended the throne, the ministers, because Suzong's tomb had a fixed date, according to rite enshrined the former empress dowager at the tomb and temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Daizong's accession year, the ministers, with Suzong's tomb date set, enshrined the former empress dowager at tomb and temple according to rite.

sentences.zh: 宰臣郭子儀等上表曰：

translations.literal: Chancellor Guo Ziyi and others submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Guo Ziyi and others submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「儷宸極者，允歸於淑德；

translations.literal: "She who matches the apex of Heaven belongs by right to virtuous conduct;
translations.idiomatic: "She who shares the throne belongs by right to virtuous conduct;

sentences.zh: 諡徽號者，必副於鴻名。

translations.literal: she who receives a posthumous title must accord with a great name.
translations.idiomatic: she who receives a posthumous title must bear a name worthy of it.

sentences.zh: 當履運而承天，則因心而追往，此先王之明訓，聖人之茂典也。

translations.literal: When one inherits the mandate and receives Heaven, one follows the heart in honoring the past—this is the bright instruction of former kings and the abundant norm of sages.
translations.idiomatic: When one inherits the mandate and receives Heaven, one honors the past from the heart—this is the bright instruction of former kings and the abundant norm of sages.

sentences.zh: 伏惟先太后圓精挺質，方祗稟秀。

translations.literal: We respectfully consider that the former empress dowager, round in essence and upright in substance, received the excellence of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully consider that the former empress dowager, pure in essence and upright in substance, received Earth's excellence.

sentences.zh: 禎符協於四星，典禮敦于萬國，得元和之正氣，韞霄漢之清英。

translations.literal: Auspicious signs accorded with the four stars; ceremonial norms were honored among ten thousand states; she obtained the correct qi of harmony and stored the clear brilliance of the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious signs matched the four stars; ceremonial norms were honored among all states; she possessed harmony's correct breath and stored the Milky Way's clear brilliance.

sentences.zh: 顧史求箴，道先於壺則；

translations.literal: Looking to history for admonition, the Way came first in the rules of the inner quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Looking to history for admonition, the Way came first in inner-court rule;

sentences.zh: 捴謙率禮，教備於中闈。

translations.literal: holding humility and leading by rite, her teaching was complete within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: holding humility and leading by rite, her teaching was complete within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 太陰無昃朓之征，丙殿有祝延之慶。

translations.literal: The great yin showed no sign of waning; in the Bing Hall there was the blessing of prayers for long life.
translations.idiomatic: The great yin showed no sign of waning; in the Bing Hall there were prayers for long life.

sentences.zh: 尊敬師傅，佩服禮經，勤於蘋藻之薦，罔貴珩璜之飾。

translations.literal: She revered her teachers, wore the rites on her person, diligently offered the water-cress and duckweed, and did not prize the ornaments of pendant and ring.
translations.idiomatic: She revered her teachers, wore the rites upon her person, diligently offered water-cress and duckweed, and did not prize pendant and ring.

sentences.zh: 徽音允穆，嘉慶聿彰，憲度輔佐之勞，緝熙玄默之化，足以光昭宗祀，作配紫微。

translations.literal: Her fine reputation was true and solemn, her good fortune brightly manifest; her labor in assisting with statutes and her silent, radiant transformation were enough to glorify the ancestral sacrifices and serve as consort to the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her fine reputation was true and solemn, her good fortune brightly manifest; her labor in assisting with statutes and her silent, radiant transformation were enough to glorify the ancestral sacrifices and serve as consort to the Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 豈《騶虞》之風，行于江、漢之域；

translations.literal: Could the wind of the 'Zou Yu' run in the domains of the Yangtze and Han;
translations.idiomatic: Could the wind of the 'Zou Yu' run in the Yangtze and Han;

sentences.zh: 《葛覃》之詠，起自岐陽之下。

translations.literal: the song of the 'Ge Tan' rise from below Mount Qi?
translations.idiomatic: the song of the 'Ge Tan' rise from below Mount Qi?

sentences.zh: 爰膺歷數，作啟聖明，大拯艱難，永清夷夏。

translations.literal: She received the succession and opened sage clarity, greatly rescued hardship, and forever cleared barbarian and Chinese alike.
translations.idiomatic: She received the succession and opened sage clarity, greatly rescued hardship, and forever cleared barbarian and Chinese alike.

sentences.zh: 雖復文母成周王之業，慶都誕帝堯之聖，異代同符，彼多慚德。

translations.literal: Though Wen Mu completed the Zhou king's enterprise and Qingdu bore Emperor Yao's sagehood, different ages bore the same sign—yet they would mostly blush at her virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wen Mu completed the Zhou king's enterprise and Qingdu bore Emperor Yao's sagehood, different ages bore the same sign—yet they would mostly blush before her virtue.

sentences.zh: 昊蒼不吊，聖善長違。

translations.literal: Great Heaven did not pity; sage goodness was long lost.
translations.idiomatic: Great Heaven did not pity; sage goodness was long lost.

sentences.zh: 當圓魄之成，玉英早落；

translations.literal: When the full orb was complete, the jade blossom fell early;
translations.idiomatic: When the full orb was complete, the jade blossom fell early;

sentences.zh: 有坤儀之美，象服未加。

translations.literal: though she had the beauty of the feminine norm, the ceremonial robes were not yet conferred.
translations.idiomatic: though she had the beauty of the feminine norm, ceremonial robes were not yet conferred.

sentences.zh: 悲懷於先遠之辰，感慟于易名之日。

translations.literal: Grief filled the time of the distant past; anguish moved the day of changing the name.
translations.idiomatic: Grief filled the time of the distant past; anguish moved the day of changing the name.

sentences.zh: 伏以山陵貞兆，良吉有期，虞祔之儀，式資配享。

translations.literal: We respectfully note that the tomb's auspicious site has a fixed, favorable date; the rite of enshrinement requires a consort for joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully note that the tomb's auspicious site has a fixed date; the rite of enshrinement requires a consort for joint sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 率由故實，敬奉嘉名。

translations.literal: Following former precedent, we respectfully offer this fine name.
translations.idiomatic: Following former precedent, we respectfully offer this fine name.

sentences.zh: 謹按諡法：『敬慎高明曰章，法度明大曰章，夙興夜寐曰敬，齊莊中正曰敬。』

translations.literal: We respectfully consult the posthumous-name law: 'Reverent, cautious, and lofty is called Zhang; clear in law and great in measure is called Zhang; rising early and sleeping late is called Jing; even, solemn, and centered is called Jing.'
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully consult the posthumous-name law: 'Reverent, cautious, and lofty is called Zhang; clear in law and great in measure is called Zhang; rising early and sleeping late is called Jing; even, solemn, and centered is called Jing.'

sentences.zh: 敢遵先典，仰圖懿德，謹上尊諡曰章敬皇后。」

translations.literal: We dare follow the former canon, look up to her excellent virtue, and respectfully submit the honored posthumous title Empress Zhangjing."
translations.idiomatic: We dare follow the former canon, look up to her excellent virtue, and respectfully submit the honored posthumous title Empress Zhangjing."

sentences.zh: 二年三月，祔葬建陵。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year she was enshrined and buried at Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year she was enshrined and buried at Jianling.

sentences.zh: 啟春明門外舊壟，后容狀如生，粉黛如故，而衣皆赭黃色，見者駭異，以為聖子符兆之先。

translations.literal: They opened the old mound outside Chunming Gate; the empress's appearance was as in life, her powder and rouge as before, and her garments were all ochre-yellow; those who saw it were startled and took it as a prior omen of the sage son's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the old mound outside Chunming Gate. The empress looked as in life, powder and rouge unchanged, and her garments were all ochre-yellow. Viewers were astonished and took it as an omen of the sage son's mandate.

sentences.zh: 后父令珪，寶應初贈太尉；

translations.literal: The empress's father Linggui was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant at the beginning of Baoying;
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoying her father Linggui was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 母李氏，贈秦國夫人。

translations.literal: her mother Lady Li was posthumously honored as Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: her mother Lady Li as Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 叔令瑤，拜太子家令，封馮翊郡公；

translations.literal: Her uncle Lingyao was appointed Tutor to the Crown Prince and enfeoffed as Duke of Fenyang;
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Lingyao was appointed Tutor to the Crown Prince and enfeoffed Duke of Fenyang;

sentences.zh: 令瑜，太子右諭德，封濟陰郡公。

translations.literal: Lingyu was Right Mentor to the Crown Prince and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyu was Right Mentor to the Crown Prince and enfeoffed Duke of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 后兄漵，鴻臚少卿，封鄄城縣公；

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Su was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was enfeoffed as Duke of Juancheng;
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Su was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and enfeoffed Duke of Juancheng;

sentences.zh: 澄，太子賓客，濮陽縣公；

translations.literal: Cheng was Companion to the Crown Prince and Duke of Puyang;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was Companion to the Crown Prince and Duke of Puyang;

sentences.zh: 湊，太子詹事，臨濮縣公；

translations.literal: Cou was Chief Administrator to the Crown Prince and Duke of Linpu;
translations.idiomatic: Cou was Chief Administrator to the Crown Prince and Duke of Linpu;

sentences.zh: 並加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: all were given the added title of Grand Master with the same rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: all were given the added title of Grand Master with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 漵位終金吾大將軍，湊位終京兆尹，見《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Su ended as General of the Gold Crow Guard; Cou ended as Intendant of Jingzhao—see the Biographies of Outer Relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Su ended as General of the Gold Crow Guard; Cou as Intendant of Jingzhao—see the Biographies of Outer Relatives.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿真皇后沈氏，吳興人，世為冠族。

translations.literal: Empress Ruizhen of Emperor Daizong, née Shen, was a native of Wuxing; her family for generations were leading clans.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ruizhen of Daizong, née Shen, came from Wuxing; her family for generations were leading clans.

sentences.zh: 父易直，秘書監。

translations.literal: Her father Yizhi was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yizhi was Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元末，以良家子選入東宮，賜太子男廣平王。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, as a woman of good family she was chosen into the Eastern Palace and given to the crown prince's son, Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyuan, as a woman of good family she was chosen for the Eastern Palace and given to the crown prince's son, Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年，生德宗皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao she bore Emperor Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 she bore Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，諸王、妃、主從幸不及者，多陷於賊，后被拘於東都掖庭。

translations.literal: When the Rebellion of An Lushan broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu; princes, consorts, and princesses who could not follow mostly fell into the rebels' hands. The empress was detained in the Eastern Capital's inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan's rebellion broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu. Princes, consorts, and princesses who could not follow mostly fell to the rebels. The empress was detained in the Eastern Capital's inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 及代宗破賊，收東都，見之，留于宮中，方經略北征，未暇迎歸長安。

translations.literal: When Daizong defeated the rebels and recovered the Eastern Capital, he saw her and kept her in the palace; he was then planning the northern campaign and had no leisure to welcome her back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong defeated the rebels and recovered the Eastern Capital, he saw her and kept her in the palace. He was then planning the northern campaign and had no leisure to bring her back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明再陷河洛。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Siming again took Henei and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Siming again took Henei and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及朝義敗，復收東都，失后所在，莫測存亡。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was defeated and the Eastern Capital was recovered again, the empress's whereabouts were lost and none could tell whether she lived or died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi was defeated and the Eastern Capital was recovered again, the empress's whereabouts were lost and none could tell whether she lived or died.

sentences.zh: 代宗遣使求訪，十餘年寂無所聞。

translations.literal: Daizong sent envoys to seek her; for more than ten years there was no word.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong sent envoys to seek her; for more than ten years there was no word.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，下詔曰：「王者事父孝，故事天明；

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne, an edict proclaimed: "When a king serves his father with filial piety, he thereby illuminates Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, an edict proclaimed, "When a king serves his father with filial piety, he thereby illuminates Heaven;

sentences.zh: 事母孝，故事地察。

translations.literal: when he serves his mother with filial piety, he thereby illuminates Earth.
translations.idiomatic: when he serves his mother with filial piety, he thereby illuminates Earth.

sentences.zh: 則事天莫先于嚴父，事地莫盛於尊親。

translations.literal: Thus in serving Heaven nothing comes before honoring the father; in serving Earth nothing surpasses honoring the parent.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in serving Heaven nothing comes before honoring the father; in serving Earth nothing surpasses honoring the parent.

sentences.zh: 朕恭承天命，以主社稷，執珪璧以事上帝，祖宗克配，園寢永終。

translations.literal: We respectfully receive Heaven's mandate and preside over the altars of soil and grain; we hold the jade scepter and disk in serving the Supreme Lord; the ancestors are properly matched, and the garden tomb is forever complete.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully receive Heaven's mandate and preside over the altars of soil and grain; we hold jade scepter and disk in serving the Supreme Lord; the ancestors are properly matched, and the garden tomb is forever complete.

sentences.zh: 而內朝虛位，闕問安之禮，銜悲內惻，憂戀終歲。

translations.literal: Yet the inner court's place stands empty, the rite of inquiring after well-being is lacking, grief fills the inner heart, and longing endures through the year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the inner court's place stands empty, the rite of inquiring after well-being is lacking, grief fills the heart, and longing endures through the year.

sentences.zh: 思欲曆舟車之路，以聽求音問，而主茲重器，莫匪深哀。

translations.literal: We wish to traverse the roads of boat and carriage to listen for word of her, yet in holding this heavy vessel none is free of deep sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to traverse roads by boat and carriage to seek word of her, yet in holding this heavy vessel none is free of deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 是用仰稽舊儀，敬崇大號，舉茲禮命，式遵前典。

translations.literal: Therefore we respectfully look to former rites, reverently raise a great title, offer this ceremonial command, and follow the former canon.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we respectfully look to former rites, reverently raise a great title, offer this ceremonial command, and follow the former canon.

sentences.zh: 宜令公卿大夫稽度前訓，上皇太后尊號。」

translations.literal: Let the high ministers and grandees examine former instruction and submit the honored title of empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Let the high ministers and grandees examine former instruction and submit the honored title of empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 建中元年十一月，遙尊聖母沈氏為皇太后，陳禮於含元殿庭，如正至之儀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jianzhong, the sacred mother Lady Shen was honored from afar as empress dowager; ceremony was performed in the court of Hanyuan Hall as at the winter solstice rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Jianzhong 1, the sacred mother Lady Shen was honored from afar as empress dowager; ceremony was performed in the court of Hanyuan Hall as at the winter solstice rite.

sentences.zh: 上袞冕出自東序門，立於東方，朝臣班於位，冊曰：「嗣皇帝臣名言：恩莫重于顧復，禮莫貴於徽號，上以展愛敬之道，下以正《春秋》之義，則祖宗之所稟命，臣子之所盡心，尊尊親親，此焉而在。

translations.literal: Wearing the imperial robe and cap, the emperor came out from the east side gate and stood in the east; court ministers took their places in rank; the investiture text read: "The succeeding emperor, your subject [Name], says: No grace is heavier than nurturing; no rite is more precious than the honored title. Above, to extend the Way of love and reverence; below, to set right the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals—then the mandate received from the ancestors and the utmost heart of subject and son, honoring the honored and cherishing the near, reside herein.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing imperial robe and cap, the emperor came out from the east side gate and stood in the east; court ministers took their ranks; the investiture text read, "The succeeding emperor, your subject [Name], says: No grace is heavier than nurturing; no rite is more precious than the honored title. Above, to extend the Way of love and reverence; below, to set right the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals—then the mandate received from the ancestors and the utmost heart of subject and son, honoring the honored and cherishing the near, reside herein.

sentences.zh: 兩漢而下，帝王嗣位，崇奉尊稱，厥有舊章。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties downward, when emperors succeeded to the throne they honored and elevated titles; there are old statutes for this.
translations.idiomatic: From the Two Han dynasties downward, when emperors succeeded they honored and elevated titles; there are old statutes for this.

sentences.zh: 永惟丕烈，敢墜前典，臣名謹上尊號曰皇太后。」

translations.literal: Ever contemplating the great achievement, we dare not fall from the former canon; your subject [Name] respectfully submits the honored title Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Ever contemplating the great achievement, we dare not fall from the former canon; your subject [Name] respectfully submits the honored title Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: 帝再拜，歔唏不自勝，左右皆泣下。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed twice, sobbing beyond control; those at his side all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed twice, sobbing beyond control; those at his side all wept.

sentences.zh: 仍以睦王述為奉迎皇太后使，工部尚書喬琳副之，候太后問至，升平公主宜備起居。

translations.literal: Prince of Mu Shu was also appointed envoy to welcome the empress dowager, with Minister of Works Qiao Lin as deputy; when word of the empress dowager arrived, Princess Shengping was to attend to her daily needs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Mu Shu was also appointed envoy to welcome the empress dowager, with Minister of Works Qiao Lin as deputy; when word of the empress dowager arrived, Princess Shengping was to attend to her daily needs.

sentences.zh: 於是分命使臣，周行天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon separate envoys were dispatched to search throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon separate envoys were dispatched to search throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，吉問至，群臣稱賀，既而詐妄。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year auspicious word arrived; the ministers offered congratulations—yet it proved false.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the next year auspicious word arrived and the ministers offered congratulations—yet it proved false.

sentences.zh: 自是詐稱太后者數四，皆不之罪，終貞元之世無聞焉。

translations.literal: From then on those who falsely claimed to be the empress dowager numbered four times; none was punished, and through the Zhenyuan reign there was no further word.
translations.idiomatic: From then on four persons falsely claimed to be the empress dowager; none was punished, and through the Zhenyuan reign there was no further word.

sentences.zh: 德宗敦崇外族，贈太后父易直太師，易直子庫部員外郎介福贈太傅，介福子德州刺史士衡贈太保，易直第二子秘書少監震贈太尉；

translations.literal: Dezong honored the maternal clan; the empress dowager's father Yizhi was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor; Yizhi's son Jiefu, Outer Court Official of the Treasury, was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor; Jiefu's son Shiheng, prefect of Dezhou, was posthumously honored as Grand Protector; Yizhi's second son Zhen, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: Dezong honored the maternal clan. The empress dowager's father Yizhi was posthumously made Grand Preceptor; his son Jiefu, Outer Court Official of the Treasury, Grand Tutor; Jiefu's son Shiheng, prefect of De Prefecture, Grand Protector; Yizhi's second son Zhen, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 時沈氏封贈拜爵者百餘人。

translations.literal: at that time more than a hundred persons of the Shen clan received enfeoffment and posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than a hundred persons of the Shen clan received enfeoffment and posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 貞元七年，詔外曾祖隋陝令沈琳贈司徒，追封徐國公，與外祖贈太師易直等立五廟，以琳為始，緣祠廟所須，官給。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan, an edict posthumously honored the empress dowager's maternal great-grandfather Shen Lin, magistrate of Shan in the Sui, as Minister of Education and posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Xu; with the maternal grandfather Yizhi, posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, five temples were established, with Lin as the founder; whatever the ancestral temples required was supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 7 an edict posthumously honored the empress dowager's maternal great-grandfather Shen Lin, Sui magistrate of Shan, as Minister of Education and Duke of Xu; with her maternal grandfather Yizhi, posthumously Grand Preceptor, five temples were established with Lin as founder; whatever the ancestral temples required was supplied by the state.

sentences.zh: 後無近屬，惟族子房為近，德宗用為金吾將軍，主沈氏之祀。

translations.literal: The empress had no close relatives; only clansman Fang was near, and Dezong employed him as General of the Gold Crow Guard to preside over the Shen sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had no close relatives; only clansman Fang was near, and Dezong employed him as General of the Gold Crow Guard to preside over Shen sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位之年九月，禮儀使奏：「太后沈氏厭代登真，於今二十七載，大行皇帝至孝惟深，哀思罔極。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the year Xianzong ascended the throne, the Commissioner of Ceremonies memorialized: "Empress Dowager Lady Shen has departed this life and ascended to truth; it is now twenty-seven years. The late emperor's filial piety was deep and his grief boundless.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xianzong's accession year, the Commissioner of Ceremonies memorialized, "Empress Dowager Lady Shen has departed this life and ascended to truth; it is now twenty-seven years. The late emperor's filial piety was deep and his grief boundless.

sentences.zh: 建中之初，已發明詔，舟車所至，靡不周遍，歲月滋深，迎訪理絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong an edict had already been issued; wherever boat and carriage reached, none was left unsearched; as months and years deepened, the search for welcome was logically exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianzhong an edict had already been issued; wherever boat and carriage reached, none was left unsearched; as months and years deepened, the search for welcome was logically exhausted.

sentences.zh: 按晉庾蔚之議，尋求三年之後，又俟中壽而服之。

translations.literal: According to Yu Wei's discussion in Jin, after three years of searching one waits for middle longevity before putting on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: According to Yu Wei's discussion in Jin, after three years of searching one waits for middle longevity before putting on mourning.

sentences.zh: 今參詳禮例，伏請以大行皇帝啟攢宮日，百官舉哀于肅章門內之正殿，先令有司造禕衣一副，發哀日令內官以禕衣置於幄。

translations.literal: Now examining rites and precedents, we respectfully ask that on the day the late emperor's coffin is placed in the temporary palace, all officials mourn in the main hall inside Suzhang Gate; first let the relevant offices prepare one set of burial garments; on the day mourning begins let inner officials place the burial garments in the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Now examining rites and precedents, we respectfully ask that on the day the late emperor's coffin is placed in the temporary palace, all officials mourn in the main hall inside Suzhang Gate; first let the relevant offices prepare one set of burial garments; on the day mourning begins let inner officials place the burial garments in the canopy.

sentences.zh: 自後宮人朝夕上食，先啟告元陵，次告天地宗廟、昭德皇后廟。

translations.literal: From then on palace women morning and evening offered food; first report to Yuanling, then report to Heaven, Earth, the ancestral temple, and Empress Zhaode's temple.
translations.idiomatic: From then on palace women morning and evening offered food; first report to Yuanling, then to Heaven, Earth, the ancestral temple, and Empress Zhaode's temple.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后諡冊，造神主，擇日祔於代宗廟。

translations.literal: Prepare the posthumous investiture and spirit tablet for the Grand Empress Dowager, choose a day, and enshrine her in Emperor Daizong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare the posthumous investiture and spirit tablet for the Grand Empress Dowager, choose a day, and enshrine her in Daizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 其禕衣備法駕奉迎於元陵祠，復置於代宗皇帝袞衣之右。

translations.literal: Prepare the burial garments with the full imperial escort to welcome them at Yuanling Shrine, then place them again to the right of Emperor Daizong's imperial robe.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare the burial garments with the full imperial escort to welcome them at Yuanling Shrine, then place them to the right of Daizong's imperial robe.

sentences.zh: 便以發哀日為國忌。」

translations.literal: Let the day mourning begins serve as the national day of remembrance."
translations.idiomatic: Let the day mourning begins serve as the national day of remembrance."

sentences.zh: 詔如奏。

translations.literal: An edict followed the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，冊諡曰睿真皇后，奉神主祔于代宗之室。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year she was invested with the posthumous title Empress Ruizhen, and her spirit tablet was enshrined in Daizong's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year she was invested with the posthumous title Empress Ruizhen, and her spirit tablet was enshrined in Daizong's chamber.

sentences.zh: 代宗崔妃，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Consort Cui of Emperor Daizong was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Cui of Daizong came from Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 父峋，秘書少監。

translations.literal: Her father Xun was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xun was Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 母楊氏，韓國夫人。

translations.literal: Her mother was Lady Yang, Lady of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was Lady Yang, Lady of Han.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，楊貴妃寵倖，即妃之姨母也。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era Consort Yang received favor; she was the consort's maternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era Consort Yang received favor; she was the consort's maternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 時韓國、虢國之寵，冠于戚里。

translations.literal: At that time the favor shown Lady of Han and Lady of Guo topped all the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the favor shown Lady of Han and Lady of Guo topped all the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 時代宗為廣平王，故玄宗選韓國之女，嬪于廣平邸，禮儀甚盛。

translations.literal: Daizong was then Prince of Guangping; Xuanzong chose Lady of Han's daughter as consort in the Prince of Guangping's residence, and the ceremonial was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was then Prince of Guangping; Xuanzong chose Lady of Han's daughter as consort in his residence, and the ceremonial was very grand.

sentences.zh: 生召王偲。

translations.literal: She bore Prince of Shao, Si.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Prince Si of Shao.

sentences.zh: 初，妃挾母氏之勢，性頗妒悍，及西京陷賊，母黨皆誅，妃從王至靈武，恩顧漸薄，達京而薨。

translations.literal: At first the consort relied on her mother's clan's power and was by nature jealous and fierce; when the Western Capital fell to the rebels her mother's faction was all executed. The consort followed the prince to Lingwu; favor gradually thinned, and she died after reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At first the consort relied on her mother's clan and was jealous and fierce. When the Western Capital fell her mother's faction was executed. She followed the prince to Lingwu; favor gradually thinned, and she died after reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗貞懿皇后獨孤氏，父穎，左威衛錄事參軍，以后貴，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenyi of Emperor Daizong, née Dugu; her father Ying was Recorder of the Left Weiwu Guard; because of the empress's honor he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenyi of Daizong, née Dugu; her father Ying was Recorder of the Left Weiwu Guard; because of her honor he was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 后以美麗入宮，嬖幸專房，故長秋虛位，諸姬罕所進御。

translations.literal: The empress entered the palace for her beauty and received exclusive favor; therefore the position of Chief of the Long Autumn stood empty, and the other ladies were rarely admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The empress entered the palace for her beauty and received exclusive favor. The position of Chief of the Long Autumn stood empty, and the other ladies were rarely admitted.

sentences.zh: 後始冊為貴妃，生韓王迥、華陽公主。

translations.literal: Later she was invested as Noble Consort and bore Prince of Han, Jiong, and Princess Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Later she was invested as Noble Consort and bore Prince Jiong of Han and Princess Huayang.

sentences.zh: 華陽聰悟過人，能候上顏色，發言必隨喜慍。

translations.literal: Huayang was clever beyond others; she could read the emperor's countenance, and whatever she said always followed his joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: Huayang was clever beyond others; she could read the emperor's countenance, and whatever she said always followed his mood.

sentences.zh: 上之所賞，則因而美之；

translations.literal: What the emperor favored, she then praised;
translations.idiomatic: What the emperor favored, she then praised;

sentences.zh: 上之所惡，則曲以全之，由是鍾愛特異。

translations.literal: what the emperor disliked, she tactfully spared—therefore love and favor were exceptionally concentrated on her.
translations.idiomatic: what he disliked, she tactfully spared—therefore love and favor were exceptionally concentrated on her.

sentences.zh: 大曆九年，公主薨，上嗟悼過深，數日不視朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dali, the princess died; the emperor's grief and lamentation were excessive, and for several days he did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 9 the princess died; the emperor's grief was excessive, and for several days he did not hold court.

sentences.zh: 宰臣等因中使吳承倩附奏，言修短常理，以社稷之重，宜節哀視事。

translations.literal: The chancellors, through the inner envoy Wu Chengqian, appended a memorial saying that length and brevity are the constant of fate and that, for the weight of the altars of soil and grain, he should restrain grief and attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors, through the inner envoy Wu Chengqian, appended a memorial saying that length and brevity are fate's constant and that, for the weight of the altars, he should restrain grief and attend to affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，公主疾，上令宗師道教，名曰瓊華真人。

translations.literal: At first, when the princess fell ill, the emperor ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan to perform Daoist teaching and gave her the name Qionghua the Perfected One.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess first fell ill, the emperor ordered the Director of the Imperial Clan to perform Daoist teaching and gave her the name Qionghua the Perfected One.

sentences.zh: 及疾亟，上親自臨視，屬纊之際，齧傷上指，其愛念如此。

translations.literal: When her illness grew critical the emperor personally visited her; at the moment of placing the silk in her mouth he bit and injured his finger—such was his love.
translations.idiomatic: When her illness grew critical the emperor personally visited her; at the moment of placing the silk in her mouth he bit and injured his finger—such was his love.

sentences.zh: 上既未聽朝，宰臣等諫曰：「公主夙成神悟，仁眷特鐘，嘗禱必親，已承減膳，幽明遽間，倍軫慈衷。

translations.literal: The emperor had not yet resumed court when the chancellors remonstrated, saying: "The princess from youth attained divine understanding; benevolent favor was especially concentrated on her. When she prayed she always did so in person; she had already accepted reduced meals. The hidden and manifest were suddenly parted, doubling the wound to your compassionate heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not yet resumed court when the chancellors remonstrated, saying, "The princess from youth attained divine understanding; benevolent favor was especially concentrated on her. When she prayed she always did so in person; she had already accepted reduced meals. The hidden and manifest were suddenly parted, doubling the wound to your compassionate heart.

sentences.zh: 臣等微誠，無由感達。

translations.literal: Our slight sincerity could not reach you.
translations.idiomatic: Our slight sincerity could not reach you.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下守累聖之公器，禦群生之重畜，夷百戰之艱患，撫四海之傷殘。

translations.literal: We respectfully consider that Your Majesty holds the public vessel accumulated by successive sages, governs the heavy charge of all living beings, smoothed the hardship of a hundred battles, and comforted the wounded of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully consider that Your Majesty holds the public vessel accumulated by successive sages, governs the heavy charge of all living beings, smoothed the hardship of a hundred battles, and comforted the wounded of the four seas.

sentences.zh: 虜候為虞，戎師近警，一言萬務，裁成聖心，得失謬於毫釐，安危存於晷刻。

translations.literal: Barbarian scouts cause alarm; border troops are near warning; in a word lie ten thousand affairs, all shaped by the sage heart; gain and loss err by a hair's breadth, and safety and peril hang on a moment's measure.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian scouts cause alarm; border troops are near warning; in a word lie ten thousand affairs, all shaped by the sage heart; gain and loss err by a hair's breadth, and safety and peril hang on a moment's measure.

sentences.zh: 伏慮顧懷猶切，神志未和，眾情以之不甯，臣子以之兢悸。

translations.literal: We fear your lingering care is still deep and spirit and harmony not yet restored; the multitude is thereby unsettled, and subjects and sons are thereby fearful.
translations.idiomatic: We fear your lingering care is still deep and spirit and harmony not yet restored; the multitude is thereby unsettled, and subjects and sons are thereby fearful.

sentences.zh: 伏願抑周喪之私痛，均品物於至公，下慰黔黎，上安宗社。」

translations.literal: We respectfully wish that you restrain the private grief of the Zhou mourning, equalize all things in utmost fairness, comfort the common people below, and settle the altars above."
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully wish that you restrain the private grief of the Zhou mourning, equalize all things in utmost fairness, comfort the common people below, and settle the altars above."

sentences.zh: 上始聽朝。

translations.literal: The emperor then resumed court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then resumed court.

sentences.zh: 大曆十年五月，貴妃薨，追諡曰貞懿皇后，殯于內殿，累年不忍出宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year of Dali the Noble Consort died; she was posthumously titled Empress Zhenyi and lay in state in the inner hall; for years the emperor could not bear to remove her from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Dali 10 the Noble Consort died; she was posthumously titled Empress Zhenyi and lay in state in the inner hall; for years the emperor could not bear to remove her from the palace.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月方葬，命宰臣常袞為哀冊曰：

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year she was finally buried; the emperor ordered Chancellor Chang Gun to compose the lamentation text:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year she was finally buried; the emperor ordered Chancellor Chang Gun to compose the lamentation text:

sentences.zh: 「維大曆十年，歲在辛卯，十月辛酉朔。

translations.literal: "In the tenth year of Dali, the year xinmao, the first day of the tenth month, xinyou.
translations.idiomatic: "In the tenth year of Dali, the year xinmao, the first day of the tenth month, xinyou.

sentences.zh: 六日丙寅，貴妃獨孤氏薨。

translations.literal: On the sixth day, bingyin, Noble Consort Lady Dugu died.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day, bingyin, Noble Consort Lady Dugu died.

sentences.zh: 粵明日，追諡曰貞懿皇后，殯于內殿之西階。

translations.literal: On the following day she was posthumously titled Empress Zhenyi and lay in state on the western steps of the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day she was posthumously titled Empress Zhenyi and lay in state on the western steps of the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 十三年十月癸酉，乃命門下侍郎、同平章事常袞持節冊命。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, on the day guiyou, the emperor ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Councillor Chang Gun to bear the staff of command and perform the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirteenth year, on the day guiyou, the emperor ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Chief Councillor Chang Gun to bear the staff of command and perform the investiture.

sentences.zh: 以其月二十五日丁酉，遷座于莊陵，禮也。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day of that month, dingyou, the seat was moved to Zhuangling—by rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth day of that month, dingyou, the seat was moved to Zhuangling—by rite.

sentences.zh: 素紗列位，黼奕周庭，輅升玉綴，軒楹珠欞。

translations.literal: Plain gauze ranks were arrayed; embroidered splendor filled the court; the carriage rose with jade trappings; the carriage curtains with pearl lattices.
translations.idiomatic: Plain gauze ranks were arrayed; embroidered splendor filled the court; the carriage rose with jade trappings; the carriage curtains with pearl lattices.

sentences.zh: 皇帝悼鸞掖以追懷，感麟跡而增慟，備百禮以殷遣，命六宮而哀送。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned the phoenix chamber in remembrance and was moved by the unicorn's trace to deeper grief; a hundred rites were prepared for a solemn send-off, and the six palaces were ordered to lament and escort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned the phoenix chamber in remembrance and was moved by the unicorn's trace to deeper grief; a hundred rites were prepared for a solemn send-off, and the six palaces were ordered to lament and escort.

sentences.zh: 宗祝薦告，司儀降收，爰詔侍臣，紀垂鴻休。

translations.literal: The ancestral priest offered report; the master of ceremony descended to receive; then the attendant ministers were commanded to record and leave this great blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral priest offered report; the master of ceremony descended to receive; then attendant ministers were commanded to record and leave this great blessing.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 『祚祉悠久，寵靈誕受，元魏戚籓，周、隋帝后。

translations.literal: 'Blessing and fortune long endure; favor and spirit received at birth; a kinsman prince of Northern Wei; empress of Zhou and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 'Blessing and fortune long endure; favor and spirit received at birth; a kinsman prince of Northern Wei; empress of Zhou and Sui.

sentences.zh: 五侯迭興，七貴居右，肇啟皇運，光膺文母。

translations.literal: Five marquises rose in succession; seven nobles stood at the right; they opened the imperial fortune and received the civil mother of culture.
translations.idiomatic: Five marquises rose in succession; seven nobles stood at the right; they opened the imperial fortune and received the civil mother of culture.

sentences.zh: 纘女是因，以綱大倫，生知陰教，育我蒸人。

translations.literal: Continuing through daughters, they bound the great human relations; born knowing the feminine teaching, they nurtured our people.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing through daughters, they bound the great human relations; born knowing the feminine teaching, they nurtured our people.

sentences.zh: 瑞雲呈彩，瑤星降神，聰明睿智，婉麗貞仁。

translations.literal: Auspicious clouds showed color; a jade star descended as spirit; intelligent, wise, and discerning; graceful, lovely, chaste, and benevolent.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious clouds showed color; a jade star descended as spirit; intelligent, wise, and discerning; graceful, lovely, chaste, and benevolent.

sentences.zh: 惟昔天監，搜求才淑，龍德在田，葛覃于穀。

translations.literal: In former times Heaven watched; talent and virtue were sought; the dragon's virtue was in the field; the 'Ge Tan' in the valley.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Heaven watched; talent and virtue were sought; the dragon's virtue was in the field; the 'Ge Tan' in the valley.

sentences.zh: 周薑胥宇，漢後推轂，王業惟艱，嬪風已穆。

translations.literal: Jiang of Zhou chose her dwelling; the Han empress pushed the carriage; royal enterprise was hard; consortly wind was already solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang of Zhou chose her dwelling; the Han empress pushed the carriage; royal enterprise was hard; consortly wind was already solemn.

sentences.zh: 繼文傳聖，嗣徽克令，不曜其光，乃終有慶。

translations.literal: Continuing culture and transmitting sagehood, inheriting brilliance and fulfilling command; not displaying her light, yet in the end there was blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Continuing culture and transmitting sagehood, inheriting brilliance and fulfilling command; not displaying her light, yet in the end there was blessing.

sentences.zh: 祗奉園寢，肅恭靈命，越在哀煢，聿追孝敬。

translations.literal: Reverently serving the garden tomb, solemnly honoring the spirit's command; in orphaned grief, pursuing filial reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently serving the garden tomb, solemnly honoring the spirit's command; in orphaned grief, pursuing filial reverence.

sentences.zh: 文織絲組，硃綠玄黃，上供祭服，以祀明堂。

translations.literal: Embroidered silk and thread, vermilion, green, black, and yellow; above, supplying sacrificial garments to serve the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered silk and thread, vermilion, green, black, and yellow; above, supplying sacrificial garments to serve the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 法度有節，不待珩璜，篇訓之制，自盈縑緗。

translations.literal: Statutes had measure and did not wait on pendant and ring; the pattern of admonition was itself full in fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes had measure and did not wait on pendant and ring; the pattern of admonition was itself full in fine silk.

sentences.zh: 敘我邦族，風於天下，始於憂勤，協成王化。

translations.literal: Ordering our clan and kin, the wind reached all under Heaven; beginning in care and diligence, it harmonized with royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Ordering our clan and kin, the wind reached all under Heaven; beginning in care and diligence, it harmonized with royal transformation.

sentences.zh: 慈厚諸女，寵臨下嫁，登進賢才，勞謙日夜。

translations.literal: Kind to all daughters, favoring them in marriage below; advancing worthy talent, laboring humbly day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Kind to all daughters, favoring them in marriage below; advancing worthy talent, laboring humbly day and night.

sentences.zh: 服繒示儉，脫簪申誡，訪問後言，宴遊夙退。

translations.literal: Wearing plain silk to show thrift, removing hairpins to give admonition; seeking counsel afterward, retiring early from feasts and outings.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing plain silk to show thrift, removing hairpins to give admonition; seeking counsel afterward, retiring early from feasts and outings.

sentences.zh: 內加群娣，動有矜誨；

translations.literal: Within, she added to the consorts; in movement there was compassionate instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Within, she added to the consorts; in movement there was compassionate instruction;

sentences.zh: 外睦諸親，泣辭封拜。

translations.literal: without, she harmonized with kin; weeping, she declined enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: without, she harmonized with kin; weeping, she declined enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 闕翟有日，親蠶俟時，忽歸清漢，言復方祗。

translations.literal: The pheasant banner had its day; the mulberry rite awaited its time; suddenly she returned to the clear Han; words again to the square Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant banner had its day; the mulberry rite awaited its time; suddenly she returned to the clear Han; words again to the square Earth.

sentences.zh: 萬乘悼懷，群臣慕思，玉衣追慶，金鈿同儀。

translations.literal: The ten thousand chariots mourned; ministers and officials yearned in thought; jade garments pursued blessing; gold hairpins shared the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The ten thousand chariots mourned; ministers and officials yearned in thought; jade garments pursued blessing; gold hairpins shared the rite.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas, grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas, grief!

sentences.zh: 去昭陽兮窅然，乘雲駕兮何在？

translations.literal: Departing Zhaoyang—how distant; riding clouds—where is she?
translations.idiomatic: Departing Zhaoyang—how distant; riding clouds—where is she?

sentences.zh: 人代宛兮如舊，炎涼倏兮已改。

translations.literal: Generations pass as if unchanged; heat and cold suddenly alter.
translations.idiomatic: Generations pass as if unchanged; heat and cold suddenly alter.

sentences.zh: 翠葆森以成列，素旗儼而相待。

translations.literal: Green canopies dense in ranks; plain banners solemnly waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Green canopies dense in ranks; plain banners solemnly waiting.

sentences.zh: 言從玉兆之貞，永牴瑤華之彩。

translations.literal: Words follow the jade omen's constancy; forever resisting the jade blossom's color.
translations.idiomatic: Words follow the jade omen's constancy; forever resisting the jade blossom's color.

sentences.zh: 別長秋之西苑，過望春兮南登，招帝子於北渚，從母后於東陵。

translations.literal: Leaving the western garden of Long Autumn, passing Wangchun and ascending south; summoning the emperor's child at the northern islet, following the empress dowager at the eastern mound.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the western garden of Long Autumn, passing Wangchun and ascending south; summoning the emperor's child at the northern islet, following the empress dowager at the eastern mound.

sentences.zh: 下土清兮動金翠，外無像兮中有馮，合簫挽以攢咽，結雲雨之淒凝。

translations.literal: Below, earth cleared; gold and emerald moved; without, no image; within, there was presence; joining pipes and pallbearers in choked sobs; gathering cloud-rain in bitter congealing.
translations.idiomatic: Below, earth cleared; gold and emerald moved; without, no image; within, there was presence; joining pipes and pallbearers in choked sobs; gathering cloud-rain in bitter congealing.

sentences.zh: 吾君感於幽期，俯層亭而望思，慘嬪媛以延踔，極容衛以盡時。

translations.literal: Our lord was moved by the hidden term; he leaned from the layered pavilion in longing; consorts and ladies grieved in lingering steps; guard and escort exhausted the time.
translations.idiomatic: Our lord was moved by the hidden term; he leaned from the layered pavilion in longing; consorts and ladies grieved in lingering steps; guard and escort exhausted the time.

sentences.zh: 搖巾袂兮遠訣，隔軒檻兮群悲，不復見兮回禦輦，傷如何兮軫睿慈。

translations.literal: Waving sleeve and hem in distant parting; separated by balcony rails—the crowd grieved; no longer seeing the returning imperial carriage—how it wounded sage compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Waving sleeve and hem in distant parting; separated by balcony rails—the crowd grieved; no longer seeing the returning imperial carriage—how it wounded sage compassion.

sentences.zh: 下蘭皋兮背芷陽，旌悠悠兮野蒼蒼，帶白花兮掩淚，衣玄帉兮斷腸。

translations.literal: Descending the orchid bank, turning from Zhiyang; banners distant over the wild expanse; wearing white flowers to cover tears; garments of dark border to break the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Descending the orchid bank, turning from Zhiyang; banners distant over the wild expanse; wearing white flowers to cover tears; garments of dark border to break the heart.

sentences.zh: 當盛明兮共樂，忽幽處兮獨傷，去故廷兮日遠，即新宮兮夜長。

translations.literal: Once in bright splendor sharing joy; suddenly in hidden place alone grieving; leaving the old court—the days distant; entering the new palace—the nights long.
translations.idiomatic: Once in bright splendor sharing joy; suddenly in hidden place alone grieving; leaving the old court—the days distant; entering the new palace—the nights long.

sentences.zh: 襚無文繡之飾，器無珠貝之藏，蓋自我之立制，刑有國之大方。

translations.literal: The burial gifts had no embroidered ornament; the vessels no pearl and shell store; this was the self-established regulation; punishment for the state's great norm.
translations.idiomatic: The burial gifts had no embroidered ornament; the vessels no pearl and shell store; this was the self-established regulation; punishment for the state's great norm.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, alas, grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, alas, grief!

sentences.zh: 見送往之空歸，歎終焉之如此，方士神兮是與非，甘泉畫兮疑復似。

translations.literal: Seeing the send-off return empty; sighing that the end was thus; was the fangshi divine—or not? did the Ganquan portrait seem so again?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the send-off return empty; sighing that the end was thus; was the fangshi divine—or not? did the Ganquan portrait seem so again?

sentences.zh: 遺音在於玉瑱，陳跡留于金所，獻萬壽兮無期，存《二南》之餘美。』」

translations.literal: Her lingering voice remained in the jade earplugs; her traces stayed in the gold place; offering ten thousand years of longevity without end; preserving the remaining beauty of the Two South.'"
translations.idiomatic: Her lingering voice remained in the jade earplugs; her traces stayed in the gold place; offering ten thousand years of longevity without end; preserving the remaining beauty of the Two South.'"

sentences.zh: 帝追思不已，每事欲極哀情。

translations.literal: The emperor's longing did not cease; in every matter he wished to express the utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's longing did not cease; in every matter he wished to express the utmost grief.

sentences.zh: 常袞當代才臣，詔為哀詞，文旨淒悼，覽之者惻然。

translations.literal: Chang Gun was a leading talent of the age; the emperor ordered him to compose the lamentation text; the wording was mournful, and those who read it were deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Gun was a leading talent of the age; the emperor ordered him to compose the lamentation text; the wording was mournful, and those who read it were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 華陽公主先葬于城東，地卑濕，至是徙葬，祔于莊陵之園，故哀詞云：「招帝子於北渚，從母后於東陵。」

translations.literal: Princess Huayang had first been buried east of the city; the ground was low and damp; at this time she was moved and enshrined in Zhuangling's garden—hence the lamentation text says: "Summoning the emperor's child at the northern islet, following the empress dowager at the eastern mound."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Huayang had first been buried east of the city on low, damp ground; at this time she was moved and enshrined in Zhuangling's garden—hence the lamentation text says, "Summoning the emperor's child at the northern islet, following the empress dowager at the eastern mound."

sentences.zh: 乃詔常參官為輓歌，上自選其傷切者，令挽士歌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor ordered regular officials to compose dirges; he personally chose those most piercing in grief and had the pallbearers sing them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered regular officials to compose dirges; he personally chose those most piercing in grief and had the pallbearers sing them.

sentences.zh: 大曆初，后寵遇無雙，以恩澤官其宗屬，叔太常少卿卓為少府監，后兄良佐太子中允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dali the empress's favor was without rival; by grace and favor offices were given to her clan; her uncle Zhuo, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Director of the Palace Workshops; the empress's elder brother Liangzuo was Crown Prince's Companion.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dali the empress's favor was without rival; by grace and favor offices were given to her clan; her uncle Zhuo, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Director of the Palace Workshops; her elder brother Liangzuo was Crown Prince's Companion.

sentences.zh: 德宗昭德皇后王氏，父遇，官至秘書監。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaode of Emperor Dezong; her father Yu reached the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaode of Dezong; her father Yu reached the post of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 德宗為魯王時，納后為嬪。

translations.literal: When Dezong was Prince of Lu he took the empress as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was Prince of Lu he took her as a consort.

sentences.zh: 上元二年，生順宗皇帝，特承寵異。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shangyuan she bore Emperor Shunzong and received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2 she bore Emperor Shunzong and received special favor.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，冊為淑妃。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended the throne she was invested as Cultivated Consort.
